chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Four [types of people] upon whom Allah, the Exalted, will look [with mercy] on the Day of Resurrection: one who cancels a debt for a regretful debtor, or relieves a distressed person, or frees a soul [from slavery], or marries an unmarried man.
ai.seo_question: What are the four deeds that God looks upon with mercy on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting that God’s special gaze (*nazar*) on the Day of Judgment is reserved for those who alleviate human hardship through four specific acts: forgiving a regretful debtor, aiding the distressed, emancipating a slave, and marrying off the unmarried. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on social welfare and the spiritual merit of removing burdens from others, linking material charity directly to divine favor.
